brief: September US headline CPI matched expectations at 0.6% month-on-month / 3.7% year-on-year, but core CPI ran hotter at 0.3%/2.6% versus a 0.2%/2.5% consensus. Shelter, the largest-weighted component, rose 0.4% after three softer prints averaging 0.2%; airline fares (+1.2%, helped by Spirit Airlines' shutdown removing competition), used vehicles (+0.7%), recreation (+0.5%) and a 9.1% gasoline jump pushed the headline up, while food, medical care and education were soft. Core monthly prints are running above the 0.17% pace needed to return annual inflation to 2%. The data lifted Fed-funds-futures odds of an October hike to 45% from about 20% pre-release, but ING argues the report probably isn't quite strong enough to push the Fed to hike in October given officials' recent no-hurry signaling after September's 25bp move. ING still forecasts a December hike then a long pause, but sees the risk skewed toward the Fed going higher before cutting. The disinflation case rests on a cooling housing market feeding into softer shelter and slowing wage growth (3% now, low-hire low-fire labor market) offsetting upside risk from Strait of Hormuz-driven fuel prices and AI data-centre buildout costs, neither of which Fed hikes can address.
